question.text: Gains on debt mutual funds purchased on or after April 1, 2023 are taxed at:

answer.text: Slab rate without indexation (always treated as short-term)

explanation.text: The Logic: Following amendments introduced by the Finance Act 2023, units of "specified mutual funds" (broadly, debt-oriented mutual funds whose equity exposure does not exceed the prescribed limit) acquired on or after 1 April 2023 are deemed to be short-term capital assets. Gains on such units are therefore taxed at the investor's applicable income-tax slab rate, irrespective of the holding period, and the earlier indexation benefit on long-term holdings is not available for purchases under this regime. The Trap: 20% with indexation, and 12.5% with or without indexation, reflect prior-regime or other-asset rules - they do not apply to post-1-April-2023 debt-fund units. A flat 15% rate is not the slab-rate equivalent. Note: The post-April-2023 debt-fund taxation rule is not stated on the cited pages of the NISM-Series-X-A Investment Adviser (Level 1) workbook, which on the pages checked discusses debt, FMP and hybrid fund features rather than the current capital-gains treatment. The framing above is general FY 2025-26 Indian income-tax knowledge.
